I feel truly grateful to be connected with Dr. Vikas Kohli and his amazing team at Child Heart Foundation for more than 9 years now. My son Arnav has been under his care for regular checkups, and the improvement we’ve seen over the years is incredible. Today, seeing Arnav talk to Dr. Kohli so comfortably, almost like friends -  really amazes me.

Dr. Kohli is not just a doctor for us; he has been like a father figure during some of the most difficult times in my life. When my own father was suffering from liver cirrhosis, he personally connected with doctors in my hometown and guided us beyond his responsibility. That kind of care and humanity is very rare.

Every time I meet him, he doesn’t just ask about reports—he talks about health, family, and even life, just like a caring elder would. That bond is something I deeply value.

I would also like to mention Sunita Mam, who is an equally wonderful and supportive personality. The entire team is doing incredible work -- helping, guiding, and supporting every child and family with genuine care.

I wholeheartedly recommend Dr. Kohli and his team. They are not just treating patients - they are touching lives. 🙏

Born in 1994, SEEDS (Sustainable Environment and Ecological Development Society) had one ultimate goal: protecting the lives and livelihoods of people exposed to disasters. Today, we persist along the same path, continuing to focus on integrating locally based approached into each of our programs. Behind this work lies a diverse SEEDS team consisting of young professionals from various development- related fields. It is governed and advised by a board of eminent academicians and practitioners from international organisations.

Over the years, this team of committed individuals, has reached out to families affected by earthquakes, floods and cyclones; restored schools and homes; and has invariably put its faith in education to build long term resilience of the communities. SEEDS continues to advocate for and work with communities across Asia to build a safer and more sustainable world.

Dr. V. K. Sharma, President.

He is a Professor of Disaster Management & Convener of the Training Advisory Committee at the Indian Institute of Public Administration (since 2006). Formerly, he was the Chief of Party, Program for Enhancement of Emergency Response (PEER), a USAID funded program for six Asian Countries.

Dr. Manu Gupta, Vice President.

He is the co-founder and director of SEEDS. His 19 years of experience in the sector covers national and regional advocacy, mobilization of community led efforts in recovery and risk reduction, climate change adaptation and emerging issues including humanitarian partnership, accountability and community resilience. He holds a doctorate degree in community based disaster management. He completed his Masters in Urban Planning and the Bachelor’s degree in Physical Planning. He currently serves as the Chair of the Asian Disaster Risk Reduction and Response Network, an active network of national NGOs from over 17 countries in Asia. He is part of the Steering Committee of the Global Network of CSOs for Disaster Reduction. He is also the Global Advisor for UN-ISDR on the Resilient Cities Campaign. He is a contributor to UN-ISDR’s Global Assessment Report, 2011; and expert reviewer for the IPCC, SREX report.
At the national level, Manu is the co-founder and member of the core group of the Alliance for Adaption & Disaster Risk Reduction in India and serves on various national committees of the Government of India

review_text:
Victoria Memorial in Kolkata is a majestic testament to India's colonial past and a stunning architectural marvel. As I stepped into its grand courtyard, I was immediately transported to a bygone era of British rule in India. The memorial's imposing white marble structure, adorned with intricate carvings and surrounded by lush gardens, exudes an air of regal elegance.

Exploring the galleries inside, I was captivated by the vast collection of paintings, sculptures, and historical artifacts that vividly depict the rich tapestry of Indian history and culture. From portraits of British monarchs to exquisite displays of Indian artistry, each exhibit offered a glimpse into the shared heritage of two nations intertwined by history.

The highlight of my visit was ascending the memorial's central dome, offering panoramic views of Kolkata's skyline against the backdrop of the Hooghly River. It was a surreal experience, standing atop this architectural masterpiece and contemplating the legacy it represents.

However, amidst the grandeur, I couldn't help but reflect on the complex colonial legacy that the Victoria Memorial embodies. While it serves as a symbol of India's cultural heritage and resilience, it also serves as a reminder of the colonial exploitation and oppression that shaped the country's history.

Overall, my visit to the Victoria Memorial was a profound and enlightening experience, offering a nuanced perspective on India's past and present. It's a must-visit destination for anyone seeking to delve into the rich tapestry of Indian history and culture.

review_text:
One of the most authentic experiences:
From our first contact with our StreetConnections guide Lalit we had such a great experience. Booking over the phone was easy, and Lalit was extremely flexible with us, accommodating a late change of the day of the booking all in his stride.
The walk itself was one of our best experiences in India. He stressed over the phone that we wouldn't be visiting any of the main tourist sites, which proved to be 100% accurate. You can do all that with a guide book - this walk takes you places you would never find otherwise.
To be taken through the backstreets of Old Delhi by someone who has taken himself from being a wily street kid (at the age of 5) to a final year university student was all the more poignant. Lalit was so generous with his time and his personal story, all the while flashing that charming smile and making plenty of jokes along the way.
If you want to see the backstreets, plus so much more that others have described here, then do yourself a favour and book a tour with these guys - 5 stars!
